Consumers trust brand endorsements and product-specific marketing claims.
Alcohol consumption is socially acceptable when done responsibly.
Describing a product as 'unbelievable' enhances its perceived value and desirability.
Using terms like 'crew' and 'hangout' implies camaraderie and shared experience as desirable contexts.
Natural flavors are considered superior or more trustworthy than artificial ones.
The listener associates premium status with high-quality ingredients and craftsmanship.
Drinking alcohol in specific settings (e.g., outdoors, parties) reinforces positive social identity.
Exaggerated language strengthens persuasive impact in promotional messaging.
Newness ('newest flavor') signals innovation and increases consumer interest.
